Relate latent class membership to external covariates

Source: R/three-step.R
r3step.Rd

r3step() regresses membership in the classes of a fitted model on covariates that were not used to define them, holding the measurement model fixed. Treating the assigned classes as known outcomes distorts the associations; the three-step approach instead treats each assignment as an imperfect indicator of the true class, with the classification-error probabilities of the fitted model built into a multinomial logit. Coefficients are changes in the log odds of a class against the reference class, the last one, holding the other covariates constant; their exponentials are odds ratios. A transition fit can also have its initial state and transitions regressed on covariates, a separate specification. The correction assumes the classification-error probabilities do not vary with the covariates within a class; the standard errors treat them as fixed and ignore the choice of class solution, so interval coverage can fall below the nominal level when the classes are poorly separated; inspect the error matrix with get_results(x, "classification_errors"). Associations are not causal effects.

Usage

r3step(
  x,
  data,
  covariates = character(),
  level = c("individuals", "groups"),
  ci_level = 0.95,
  vcov_type = c("robust", "observed"),
  adjust = c("BH", "holm", "hochberg", "hommel", "bonferroni", "BY", "none"),
  by_group_class = FALSE,
  initial_covariates = character(),
  transition_covariates = character()
)

Arguments

x

A covariate-free fit without weights or a noise component: from multilpa() (the profile family), from lta(), or a trajectory model from mixture_regression() that classifies persons. A default lta() fit takes covariates or the Markov covariates; one with occasion-specific or second-order transitions, occasion-specific measurement, or ordinal or count indicators takes the Markov covariates only. Refused: fits with membership covariates, multilevel growth mixtures (cluster), the other multilpa() families, observation-level mixture regressions and stayer-class fits.

data

The data frame carrying the covariates, in the fit's row order; columns shared with the fit are checked row by row.

covariates

Names of numeric columns, complete and finite, that are not indicators of x. For level = "groups" each must be constant within a group; for a trajectory model, constant within a person and not part of the trajectory regression.

level

"individuals" (default) predicts profile membership, "groups" group-class membership. A trajectory model predicts its person classes, reported as level = "persons" with outcomes class_1, class_2 and so on.

ci_level

Confidence level of the intervals (default 0.95).

vcov_type

"robust" (default): the sandwich clustered on the independent units (the fit's groups; the persons of a trajectory model or a transition chain), which needs more units than the regression has coefficients, "observed" remaining available otherwise. "observed": the observed information, treating every observation as independent in the pooled regression; with by_group_class = TRUE, the model-based variance of the two-level likelihood.

adjust

Multiplicity correction across the covariate terms of every non-reference class (not the intercepts), a stats::p.adjust() method; "BH" by default.

by_group_class

FALSE (default): one pooled multinomial logit with one intercept per profile. TRUE: the two-level form of the one-step model, with profile intercepts per group class, slopes shared across group classes, and the group-class proportions estimated jointly; the group classes then capture between-group differences in membership the covariates do not explain. Only for level = "individuals" on a multilpa() fit.

initial_covariates, transition_covariates

For an lta() fit with one group class: covariates of the profile at the first occasion (constant within a person) and of every transition (read at the destination occasion, so they may vary over occasions). Either one fits the three-step latent Markov model (see Transition fits) instead of the occasion-by-occasion profile regression; covariates, level and by_group_class are refused then.

Value

A data frame with one row per non-reference class and term: level, outcome, term, estimate, standard_error, statistic, p_value, p_adjusted (NA on the intercept rows), conf_low and conf_high. Coefficients are log odds against the last class, named in the reference_class attribute; vcov_type and adjust are attributes too. With by_group_class = TRUE there is one intercept row per group class and non-reference profile, then the shared slopes and, at level = "groups", the group-class logits, with the attributes by_group_class and log_likelihood.

With initial_covariates or transition_covariates, one row per coefficient of the step-three chain: block ("initial" or "transition"), from (the origin profile, NA for an initial logit), to, term and the estimate columns (p_adjusted on the covariate terms), with the attributes log_likelihood, classification_errors (the step-two error matrix, rows the true profile), vcov_type and adjust. Initial logits are against the last profile, transition logits against staying, as in lta(initial_covariates =, transition_covariates =).

Transition fits

With covariates and level = "individuals", an lta() fit is treated occasion by occasion: the covariates predict the marginal profile at each occasion, with the scores clustered by group under "robust". That is not a model of the initial state or the transitions.

With initial_covariates or transition_covariates, each occasion is classified from its own indicators by the transition fit's measurement model (with the profile shares pooled over occasions) and assigned to its modal profile; step three is a hidden Markov model for those assignments with the classification errors fixed and the initial and transition logits regressed on the covariates. The transition fit's own posteriors are not used, because they draw on a person's other occasions and their errors would not be independent across occasions as step three assumes. The step-one fit must have one group class and no covariates. The step-three chain is homogeneous and first order, even when the step-one transition structure varies over occasions or has higher order. It uses one classification-error matrix pooled over occasions. Step-one occasion-specific measurement is refused because its error probabilities can change over occasions.

Boundary estimates

A step-three logit with a coefficient exceeding 20 in centred, scaled design coordinates, or an average class probability at or below 1e-6 over the contributing design rows, is treated as separated or on a boundary. Wald inference is refused for that regression, under both covariance types; changing the covariance estimator does not make the boundary regular.

See also

three_step() for a distal outcome; multilpa(profile_covariates = ) for the one-step alternative.

Examples

set.seed(21)
g <- rep(seq_len(50), each = 12)
x <- rnorm(600)
truth <- 1L + as.integer(runif(600) < plogis(-0.3 + 1.2 * x))
example_data <- data.frame(
  g = g, x = x,
  a = rnorm(600, ifelse(truth == 2L, 1.2, -1.2)),
  b = rnorm(600, ifelse(truth == 2L, 1.2, -1.2))
)
fit <- multilpa(example_data, c("a", "b"), "g", n_profiles = 2,
                n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 4, seed = 1)
r3step(fit, example_data, "x")
#>         level   outcome        term   estimate standard_error statistic
#> 1 individuals profile_1 (Intercept) -0.5703958      0.1191748 -4.786212
#> 2 individuals profile_1           x  1.2188658      0.1268352  9.609839
#>        p_value   p_adjusted   conf_low  conf_high
#> 1 1.699583e-06           NA -0.8039741 -0.3368175
#> 2 7.266244e-22 7.266244e-22  0.9702734  1.4674582

# Three-step regression of transition probabilities on covariates.
moves <- lta(course_engagement,
             vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),
             id = "student", n_profiles = 2, time = "sequence", n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
r3step(moves, course_engagement, transition_covariates = "sequence")
#>        block      from        to        term     estimate standard_error
#> 1    initial      <NA> profile_1 (Intercept)  0.547155214     0.20869296
#> 2 transition profile_1 profile_2 (Intercept) -1.850705801     0.28098481
#> 3 transition profile_1 profile_2    sequence -0.003170648     0.03170193
#> 4 transition profile_2 profile_1 (Intercept) -1.630640960     0.30703090
#> 5 transition profile_2 profile_1    sequence  0.011857160     0.03415178
#>    statistic      p_value p_adjusted   conf_low   conf_high
#> 1  2.6218192 8.746182e-03         NA  0.1381245  0.95618591
#> 2 -6.5864976 4.503228e-11         NA -2.4014259 -1.29998569
#> 3 -0.1000143 9.203329e-01  0.9203329 -0.0653053  0.05896400
#> 4 -5.3109995 1.090256e-07         NA -2.2324105 -1.02887145
#> 5  0.3471901 7.284485e-01  0.9203329 -0.0550791  0.07879342
